tracks.narration: You push charge onto a capacitor — where does the energy actually go?
Adding charge raises the voltage. The next little bit of charge has to be pushed against an already higher voltage — so the work piles up.
Plot voltage against charge — a straight line from zero up to V. The total work is the area under that line, a triangle with area one half Q V.
Substitute Q equals C V and you get one half C V squared. Substitute V equals Q over C and you get Q squared over two C. Same energy, three shapes.
The energy lives in the electric field between the plates — it stays there until something gives it somewhere to go.
